content:
Spatial reasoning — inside and outside, left and right, positions in a line — is where Class 1 children first learn to describe exactly where things are. It is also where a careless left-for-right costs a mark. Here is what is tested, the facts, the traps, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 1 Spatial Reasoning Olympiad tests

  • Inside / outside and near / far
  • Left and right, top and bottom
  • Ordinal positions (1st, 2nd, 3rd …) in a row or queue
  • Position and direction

Key facts your child should know

  • Always check which end you count from — left or right, front or back.
  • Positions have their own words: 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th and so on.
  • Left is the side of your left hand; right is the side of your right hand, when you face the same way as the picture.
  • Inside means within the boundary; outside means beyond it.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Counting a position from the wrong end (3rd from the left is not 3rd from the right).
  • Swapping left and right when the figure faces you.
  • Missing the difference between "next to" and "in front of / behind".

quiz.title: IMO Class 1 Spatial Reasoning Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: From Sia's house, the library is 6 steps away and the market is 11 steps away. Which is nearer, and by how many steps?
questions.explanation: 6 steps is less than 11 steps, so the library is nearer — by 11 − 6 = 5 steps.

questions.q: In a line from left to right: cap, shoe, sock, belt, glove. Which one is between the sock and the glove?
questions.explanation: Only one thing sits between the sock and the glove — the belt.

questions.q: In a row of children, how many children are there between the 2nd one and the 5th one?
questions.explanation: Count the places after 2nd and before 5th: 5 − 2 − 1 = 2.

questions.q: Piled up from bottom to top: gold coin, silver coin, copper coin, shiny coin. How many things are above the copper coin?
questions.explanation: Count the ones named after the copper coin: shiny coin — that is 1.

questions.q: Stacked from bottom to top: thick pillow, soft pillow, flat pillow, striped pillow, dotted pillow. How many things are below the flat pillow?
questions.explanation: Count the ones named before the flat pillow: thick pillow, soft pillow — that is 2.

questions.q: Stacked from bottom to top: maths book, drawing book, story book, rhyme book, sticker book. How many things are below the rhyme book?
questions.explanation: Count the ones named before the rhyme book: maths book, drawing book, story book — that is 3.

questions.q: A pile is made from bottom to top: maths book, drawing book, story book, rhyme book, sticker book. Which one is 4th from the top?
questions.explanation: The top one is the sticker book. Counting down 4 places gives the drawing book.

questions.q: Piled up from bottom to top: red book, blue book, green book, yellow book, pink book. How many things are above the red book?
questions.explanation: Count the ones named after the red book: blue book, green book, yellow book, pink book — that is 4.

questions.q: Stacked from bottom to top: big box, brown box, white box, small box. How many things are below the white box?
questions.explanation: Count the ones named before the white box: big box, brown box — that is 2.

questions.q: Anya stands 1st from the right in a line of 11 children. What is her place from the left?
questions.explanation: From the left: 11 + 1 − 1 = 11. Anya is 11th from the left.

faq.q: How do you find an ordinal position?
faq.a: Decide which end to start from, then count along: the first item is 1st, the next 2nd, and so on.

faq.q: Why do left and right get confused?
faq.a: When a figure faces you its left is on your right. Turn to face the same way as the figure to get it right.
